whitespace-remover.formula:
Options apply in this order:

1. Remove ALL whitespace: text with every \s removed -> done.
2. Remove tabs: each tab becomes one space.
3. Remove line breaks: every run of line breaks becomes one space.
4. Collapse multiple spaces: runs of 2+ spaces become one space.
5. Trim each line: leading and trailing spaces removed per line.
6. Remove empty lines: blank lines dropped.

characters removed = input length - output length

Example (trim + collapse + remove-empty):
  input: '  hello   world  \n\nfoo  ' (24 chars)
  1. collapse: ' hello world \n\nfoo ' (19 chars)
  2. trim lines: 'hello world\n\nfoo' (16 chars)
  3. remove empty: 'hello world\nfoo' (15 chars)
  removed: 24 - 15 = 9 characters
howTo: Paste your messy text into the input box.
Switch on the cleanups you need: trim lines, collapse spaces, remove empty lines, and more.
Watch the result and the removed-character counter update live.
Copy the cleaned text or download it as a .txt file.
keyFacts: Whitespace means spaces, tabs, and line breaks - the invisible characters.
Trimming removes leading and trailing spaces from every line.
Collapsing turns runs of multiple spaces into a single space.
Removing empty lines deletes blank lines but keeps the rest.
Removing line breaks merges everything into one flowing paragraph.
Remove-all deletes every whitespace character, joining all words together.

limitations: Only touches whitespace - it cannot fix spelling, grammar, or wrong words.
Remove-all joins words together with no separators; use it only when that is intended.
It cannot distinguish meaningful indentation (like code) from accidental spaces.
Non-breaking spaces and other exotic whitespace are treated as regular spaces by some steps.

The result updates live with a counter showing exactly how many characters were removed. whitespace-remover.workedExample:
Input (showing spaces as dots for clarity):
..hello...world..

foo..

Options: trim lines ON, collapse spaces ON, remove empty lines ON.

Step by step:
1. Input length: 17 + 2 (line breaks) + 5 = 24 characters.
2. Collapse multiple spaces: '..hello...world..' -> '.hello.world.'
   Result: '.hello.world.\n\nfoo.' (19 chars).
3. Trim each line: '.hello.world.' -> 'hello.world', 'foo.' -> 'foo'.
   Result: 'hello world\n\nfoo' (16 chars).
4. Remove empty lines: the blank line is dropped.
   Result: 'hello world\nfoo' (15 chars).

Characters removed: 24 - 15 = 9.
Final output:
hello world
foo
mistakes: Removing every space to 'clean' a sentence — you get one unreadable mega-word; collapse, do not annihilate.
Stripping indentation from code — Python and YAML depend on it, and your code breaks silently.
Collapsing spaces inside quoted strings — 'hello   world' in code changes meaning when the spaces matter.
Running it on poetry or ASCII art — the spacing IS the formatting; removing it destroys the work.
Assuming it fixes alignment — it removes characters, it does not re-justify or re-indent anything.
